subject: Creativity
title: SCAMPER: Seven Creative Triggers
description: A 60-second lesson on SCAMPER: Seven Creative Triggers.

hook.text: Stuck on a problem? Ask seven questions: Substitute, Combine, Adapt, Modify, Put to other use, Eliminate, Reverse.

buildup.text: Bob Eberle created SCAMPER in the 1970s. Each letter is a prompt that forces your thinking in a new direction.

discovery.text: Netflix 'eliminated' physical stores. Uber 'put to other use' personal cars.

twist.text: SCAMPER works because every innovation in history is really a variation of these seven operations. There are no others.

climax.text: Reverse alone has produced countless breakthroughs — self-service restaurants, user-generated content, open-source.

punchline.text: Seven questions. Every innovation in history. That's the toolkit.

quiz.question: What does the 'R' in SCAMPER stand for?

details.summary: SCAMPER is a checklist of seven creative operations: Substitute, Combine, Adapt, Modify, Put to another use, Eliminate, and Reverse. Applied to any existing product or idea, each trigger generates new variations and possibilities systematically.
details.whyItMatters: SCAMPER transforms the intimidating blank page into a structured checklist. It is one of the most practical and immediately usable creative thinking tools available.
takeaways: Each letter represents a specific creative transformation
SCAMPER works by modifying existing ideas rather than creating from nothing
It is particularly effective for product innovation and improvement

faq.question: How do you use SCAMPER in practice?
faq.answer: Take an existing product or idea and systematically apply each of the seven operations. Ask what could be substituted, combined with something else, adapted from another domain, modified in size or shape, and so on through the list.

faq.question: Who created SCAMPER?
faq.answer: Bob Eberle developed SCAMPER in the 1970s, building on Alex Osborn's earlier brainstorming checklists. It has since become one of the most widely taught creative thinking tools in education and business.
